note: Calame et al. (2023) identified 20 individuals whose phenotypes split between NDDs and CMT2 based on variant type and domain.

evidence.text: Calame et al. (2023) identified 20 individuals with heterozygous DHX9 variants where phenotypes ranged across distinct disease spectra from NDDs to distal symmetric polyneuropathy axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2), driven by different variant mechanisms (e.g. NLS missense vs CMT2-associated missense).

source.title: Monoallelic variation in DHX9, the gene encoding ... - PubMed
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Using exome sequencing and family-based rare-variant analyses, we identified 20 individuals with de novo, ultra-rare, heterozygous missense or loss-of-function (LoF) DHX9 variant alleles. Phenotypes ranged from NDDs to the distal symmetric polyneuropathy axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2).

evidence.text: Variants in specific domains of DHX9, such as the winged helix and C-terminal RGG domains, associate specifically with CMT2 / hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy rather than core NDD phenotypes.

source.title: The role of DEAD-and DExH-box RNA helicases in neurodevelopmental disorders
source.quote: in the winged helix and the C-terminal RGG domains of DHX9 which associate with hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy (also known as Charcot–Marie Tooth type 2 disease).
